turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on much and many?
turns.tutor:
Sure. Let me think aloud with an example: "There are ___ cars in the street."
Step 1: Can I count cars? Yes: one car, two cars, three cars.
Step 2: Things I can count take "many". So: "There are many cars in the street."
Rule: use "many" for things you can count and "much" for things you can't count.
Right: "She has many friends." Wrong: "She has much friends."
Your turn. Write much or many:
How ___ bottles are there?
